lessons: Putting all the cash into three momentum leaders with positive 20d/60d returns and prices above the 50d average beat SPY this week (+1.35% vs +0.68%), and holding afterwards instead of churning was the right call. Spread costs of $0.92 are about as big as our gap to SPY, so holding longer and limiting rotation matters. Confidence levels haven't separated good trades from bad ones yet (5 trades across the tournament), so I'm keeping them modest. The META fill was logged above its buy limit (722.34 vs 720), which shouldn't happen and may be a logging or fill problem.
self_assessment: Beat SPY this week (+1.35% vs +0.68%) holding PLTR, META and AMD, but still slightly behind since start (+0.33% vs +0.41%) after spread costs.

lessons: The CRM dip-in-uptrend entry was disciplined and correctly passed on news-driven drops (VZ/T). But holding ~85% cash meant the strategy trailed SPY in a rising week. Costs are large compared with the tiny position. The CRM fill (228.72) came in above its 222.5 limit, which needs watching. Next week: spread across 2-4 clean setups in liquid, tight-spread names, and use sensible limit prices.
self_assessment: Strategy B: +0.14% vs SPY +0.68%. Good setup selection, but too much cash and high spread costs. Next week: diversify across a few dips and trade liquid, tight-spread names.

lessons: Strategy C made no trades this week, so it trailed SPY by 0.68%. All three holds were defensible one at a time, but the T/VZ drop on SpaceX competition fears (-8 to -9% on a speculative, long-term story) was exactly the overreaction this strategy is meant to look for. It was dismissed with "no edge". The new notes say what a valid setup looks like, allow small starter positions at confidence 5-6, and make the trader treat all-0.0% prices as stale data, not as a lack of opportunities.
